Container.Name: isputnik
Container.Overview:
Private self-hosted family media library, now in Beta (4.0.0 and later). Audiobooks with a built-in player, ebooks with an in-browser reader, and a photo and video gallery with face recognition (the isputnik-faces container beside it, nothing leaves your server), albums, slideshows rendered to MP4, and a Photo Inbox for scans and photos from relatives. The family writes its own stories and recipes around what the house holds, and keeps a family tree linked to the people found in the photos. Multiple accounts with per-person progress and permissions, sharing and guest links, passkeys and two-factor sign-in, an installable PWA with offline listening, and an English or Russian interface.
Beta means your data is looked after: the database migrates itself forward on every upgrade, a copy of it is saved before each new version starts, and backups can be scheduled from the Control panel. Features are still moving. On first run, open the web UI on your home network to create the administrator account.
Container.Changes:
### 2026.11.24 — 4.92.0 Video settings on two pages, and pictures of how things work - **Videos has two tabs: Video Streaming and Video Downloads.** Everything about watching is on one page and everything about downloading on the other, in place of one Settings tab with pages behind it. Each opens with a small diagram of what the server does — play the film as it is, use a kept copy, or convert it — so the settings under it make sense. The diagrams are left out on tablets and phones. - **Hardware & transcoding, led by the hardware test.** One row shows the GPU, the CPU, memory and the disk cache; under it, the kinds of film this server converts fast enough to watch, lit only once the test has run; and beside it the settings the test recommends. **Viewers at once** says what the test measured. - **Choose where video is kept, in the app.** Disk & memory has a **Change** button that picks the folder for converted video and download copies — beside your libraries, on the cache disk or on another disk — with the same folder picker as Add library. It no longer has to be set on the container. Room for kept video and memory for converting are sliders with a number you can type, and unused video can be removed after 7, 30, 90 or 365 days. Needs the video add-on 0.42. - **Video Downloads says what is happening.** The queue, download copies, titles kept ready and the room they share in one row, with what is next; then the rules — when copies are prepared, how many at once, how many each member may have waiting, and the speed away from home. A member's own download now says its place in the queue and about how long is left. - **One Maps page.** Offline maps, photo place names, sign-in locations and road routes are set on System Settings › Maps, with what each adds and which pages use it. Gallery, Stories and Family Tree link to it and show how each feature stands. - **How phone backup works, on Device Sync.** A diagram of the four checks a photo passes — allowed network, signed in, room left, not already stored — and what happens when one says no. A check turns amber while it is stopping a phone, with a button to that phone or to adding a network. - **How this server is protected, on the Security overview.** The four layers that matter most — proxy, IP auto-block, two-factor and sign-in alerts — each with how it is set, its grade and what it stops, above the Protection level. - **Security & Members in two sections.** The group opens on a page listing **User Management** (Users, Groups, Invite links, App access) and **Security Policies** (Overview, Policies, Trusted networks, Blocked IPs); each section has its own row of tabs. **Sign-ins** and **Sign-in locations** are tabs on the Dashboard now. Old bookmarks still land on the right page, except that the Security group's own address opens the new list. - **Russian.** Converting video is called «преобразование» everywhere in the control panel, and the new pages were read through in Russian.
### 2026.11.22 — 4.91.0 Libraries page by page, one shape for every application - **Libraries, easier to find and to set up.** Libraries & Scanning › Libraries has a button per type — All, Gallery, Video, Ebooks, Audiobooks, Personal — each with its count, in place of the type dropdown; the list shows twenty at a time, and a right-click anywhere on a row opens its menu. Scanning and where the files live sit beside the list. A library's own page is four sections — General, Access, Scanning and Advanced — with one row per setting that says what it is set to now and an Edit that opens that one setting, so nothing hides inside another dialog any more. The way a book library reads its folders is called **Scanning rules** everywhere, and the Add library step is **Folder structure**. - **One access window, as a table.** Who can see a library, album or collection is a table of people and groups with their role beside each. The role menu lists every role with what it allows, then Deny access and Remove access; tick several rows to change them together. Changes are saved as you make them. - **Every application's Overview in the same shape.** Gallery, Videos, Ebooks, Audiobooks, Stories, Family Tree and Games each open on cards for what they hold, then Visibility & access, Features with their switches, their tools, and Activity & troubleshooting. The Organize tabs are gone — an application's tools are on its Overview, and Video genres, Book categories, Duplicate cleanup, Missing photos and Video streaming are pages under it; old addresses still lead to the right place. Backups are on Infrastructure › Services, where each server and container has its own. Sign-in locations moved under its map on Security, and Road routes to Stories › Settings. Offline maps gained a **Kept maps** row with Clear, which empties the kept maps and leaves keeping them on. - **Diagnostics and Logs, the same for every part.** This server's Diagnostics page has the video container's shape — Overview, Tests, Server log and Reports — and so do Games and Faces while they answer. Infrastructure › Logs shows this server's own log lines beside its events, as it already did for a container, and the two are named apart: **Events** is what someone was recorded doing, **Server log** is what the program printed. - **Live sessions say what is being converted, and why.** Each stream on Diagnostics › Video shows Video, Audio and Subtitles rows: what the file has, what the player is sent, and which steps the graphics card does. This needs a current video container; an older one shows the cards as before. Now playing was the same list on a second page, so it joined Live sessions — its button, the Dashboard's link and the old address all open it. - **Personal libraries: the location and the switch are separate.** Storage's Personal libraries row used to lead to the top of Device Sync with nothing open. It now opens the window that says where personal libraries are made; the location is a row of its own, and the switch stays off until one is chosen. Device Sync looks the same whether phone backup is set up or not — the Phone backup tile says Off and what it is waiting for. - **Under the hood.** Seven places that tidied a folder path, an address or a category name now do it in a single pass. Each input was already limited in length, so nothing was exposed, but the old way could be made slow by a long run of one character.
### 2026.11.20 — 4.90.1 Security updates for bundled libraries - **Security updates for bundled libraries.** The part of the server that hands out the app's own files now uses patched versions of two file-matching libraries that had published denial-of-service advisories. Nothing here ever passed them input from outside the app, so no one was exposed, but the fixed versions are in. The tools that check the code before each build were updated for the same reason.
### 2026.11.17 — 4.90.0 A clearer control panel, Diagnostics for every part - **The control panel, redrawn as cards.** Each application's Overview opens on a status banner over cards for what it uses — its libraries, connection, access and storage — and its Settings and Organize tabs are cards too. Device Sync is one page with its statistics; Storage is grouped by what the files are to the family, with library locations by drive and personal libraries as rows; and one access window, with switches, now grants access everywhere. Pairing a container walks you through setup steps until it is paired, then shows a summary. Every page starts with the same back line — Back, then where the page sits — and buttons follow one standard. - **Diagnostics for every part.** Infrastructure › Diagnostics has a page for this server and for each container beside it, with a report you can save (the last ten are kept) and private details left out unless you switch them on. This server can test its folders, its last backup and its disks; logging can be raised for a while and goes back on its own. The video container's page shows its hardware and formats, what is being watched right now with live graphs, and its GPU tests. - **Now playing and the hardware test for video.** Videos has a Now playing page, showing each stream as it plays. The video container's hardware test measures conversion speed, how many conversions run at once and how fast its disks are (video container 0.41.0). A library's metadata pass shows while it waits or runs, the film grid fills the page, and a film has a way back to its list. - **An album shared with you shows all of it, wherever you open it.** Someone who sees only the photos of the people shared with them opened an album sent to them from Gallery and saw just the photos with those people in it; only For you showed the whole album. Gallery › Albums, the album's page, its download, Review mode, an album block in a story, the home feed and the TV now all show what the album share opens — never more than its sender may share — and Review mode and story album blocks also show the photos you see by person when the album was not sent to you. - **Thumbnails of what was shared with you.** A photo, an audiobook or an ebook shared with you from a library you can't open opened fine but its tile was a broken image, in the album, in For you and in the lightbox. Its cover, preview and the faces on it now show, and stop showing soon after the share is withdrawn. - **A slideshow's movie plays only for someone who may see every photo in it.** The rendered movie has every photo in it and can't leave one out, but anyone who could see one of the slideshow's photos could play or download it. Now only its creator, an admin, or someone who may see all its photos gets the movie, as it already was on a TV; everyone else plays the slideshow live with the photos they may see. - **The app opens much lighter.** Its scripts and styles were sent uncompressed, and a browser asked for them again on every visit: a first visit downloaded about 1.9 MB. They are now sent compressed and kept by the browser until a release changes them, the control panel's text loads only when the control panel opens, and Home fetches the ebook reader and the photo viewer once it has appeared rather than before. A first visit is now about 300 KB, and later ones download almost nothing until the next release. Reading downloaded books offline works as before. - **Fixes.** Home asks once for what to continue, shows a poster per title, and says so when a row could not load. Dialogs no longer scroll the page sideways, values on a phone no longer break mid-word, arrow keys move through every row of tabs, and Security's policy names no longer break in a narrow table. No database changes need anything from you: one new table, for saved reports, is created on start.
### 2026.11.13 — 4.89.1 A damaged ebook no longer stops the scan - **One damaged EPUB no longer stops the whole ebook library scan.** A book whose zip was broken ("Invalid CEN header") opened without complaint and failed only when the scanner read the first file inside it, where nothing caught the error: the scan stopped, every retry hit the same book, and the library ended on **scan error**. A book that can't be read is now added with its title taken from its file name and no cover, and any other error in a single book is logged and skipped, so one book can never stop the scan again. Thanks to Stefan Knol for tracking it down.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Port used to access the iSputnik web interface.

Config.Name: Config & Data
Config.Description: Stores database, metadata, thumbnails, backups, settings, and application data. Backups appear here under backups/.

Config.Name: Media Storage
Config.Description: Media storage path. Must be Read/Write — uploading photos/videos and filing them into dated folders writes here (scanning alone only needs read). Additional storage locations can be added later by editing the container or from within iSputnik.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the app runs as. The server runs unprivileged (not root); on first start it takes ownership of the Config & Data path as this user. 99 (nobody) matches the default owner of an Unraid appdata share — leave it unless your share is owned by a different user.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the app runs as. 100 (users) matches the default group of an Unraid appdata share — leave it unless your share uses a different group.

Config.Name: App URL
Config.Description: The address the app is reached at (for example https://isputnik.example.com). Set this when you put a reverse proxy or tunnel in front: it fixes the browser origin the app accepts, and an https address is also what turns on HTTPS-only enforcement (HSTS). Leave blank for plain LAN access.

Config.Name: HSTS
Config.Description: Leave blank. When App URL starts with https:// the app tells browsers to stay on HTTPS for a year. Set to false to suppress that — for example when your reverse proxy already sends its own Strict-Transport-Security header. Nothing is sent for a plain-http App URL either way.

Config.Name: Cookie Secure
Config.Description: Leave on auto: secure cookies then follow App URL — on when it starts with https://, off for a plain http home install. Set true or false only to override that. Secure cookies are never sent over plain http, so forcing true on an http install drops the sign-in cookie and you cannot log in. (auto needs version 1.13.3 or newer.)

Config.Name: Session Length (days)
Config.Description: Number of days a login session remains valid.

Config.Name: Linked Device Session Length (days)
Config.Description: Number of days a TV, wall display or other screen signed in with Link a device stays signed in. Each one is listed under Profile, Devices and can be revoked there.

Config.Name: Invite Validity (days)
Config.Description: Number of days invitation links remain valid.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxy Addresses
Config.Description: The reverse proxy's own IP or CIDR range, comma-separated for several (e.g. 172.18.0.0/16 for a Docker network). Preferred over Trusted Proxy Hops: forwarded headers are only believed when they come from these addresses. Leave blank for direct LAN access. Needed for correct per-IP rate limiting, auto-block, and trusted networks.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxy Hops
Config.Description: Alternative to Trusted Proxy Addresses when the proxy's IP isn't fixed: the number of reverse proxies in front of the app (usually 1 behind a reverse proxy or Cloudflare Tunnel). Leave blank for direct LAN access or when Trusted Proxy Addresses is set (addresses win if both are). Set it to match your proxy count, no higher, and don't expose the app's port directly.
